chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Taliqani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi narrated that Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

He (a.s.) said: I asked him about the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'Why did the people turn away from him to others, even though they knew his superiority, his precedence, and his rank with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (a.s.) replied: 'They turned away from him to others, even though they knew his superiority, because he had killed a large number of their fathers, grandfathers, brothers, uncles, maternal uncles, and close relatives who fought against God and His Messenger. And because of that, their grudge against him was in their hearts, so they did not like him to be their ruler. And they did not have such a feeling in their hearts towards others, because he was not like them in jihad in the presence of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family). Therefore, they turned away from him and inclined towards others.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the people turn away from Imam Ali (a.s.) despite knowing his superiority?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) elucidates that the political shift from Imam Ali (a.s.) was driven by deep-seated tribal resentment rather than a denial of his merit; Ali’s decisive role in killing numerous kinsmen of the Quraysh during the early battles created a lasting psychological barrier to their allegiance. This narrative highlights the interplay between spiritual authority and social dynamics in early Islamic history, illustrating how personal vendettas could overshadow recognition of divine leadership.
